payload.body: ISSUE:0004 at a6c99b1, one finding to fix before it lands; the rest is green so far. The signer's listing check cannot see AppleDouble members on macOS. macOS bsdtar's tar reader folds every ._name entry into the next entry as Mac metadata (its mac-ext option, on by default), so bsdtar -tzf never lists them. An archive carrying a ._ccusage member, or any ._ entry, passes 'exactly the four files' and is signed and published; the Python refused it (S05, 'Unexpected archive member'). My S05 copy of the real v0.1.5 assets was refused only because its binary is ad-hoc signed. Repro, added to a scratch copy of tests/macos.bats, red as landed: @test "archives with an AppleDouble member are refused" { local from=$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stage-aarch64-apple-darwin; printf 'not metadata' > "$from/._ccusage"; COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 arm -C "$from" LICENSE README.md ._ccusage ccusage ccusage-logo.svg; finalize; refused "Unexpected release archive member"; }. Fix, green with the whole suite: in unpack, list with bsdtar --options '!mac-ext' -tzf (line 102). Adding the same option to the extract on line 113 also makes the found-count check a second guard. CI's archives stay fine: v0.1.5's passed the Python's member check, so they carry no ._ entries. Green at a6c99b1 in a fresh clone: check all, test all, build, doctor (no version note), release check, the 0.1.6 dry run (gh reads only), the 0.1.5 dry run refused, no Python/tools/xtask/workspace/keychain-upgrade left. The real v0.1.5 release verifies through a read-only gh shim, and all 12 faulted copies are refused. formula render v0.1.5 gives the tap's exact arm and Intel sha256 and refuses a draft holding only SHA256SUMS.ci. Nit, no action needed unless it matters to you: on macOS the logo now installs to libexec, not share/ccusage, while Linux keeps pkgshare; nothing in the repo reads it. Mutation pass on the zsh checks is running; results follow.
